text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Tobacco: a nonjudgmental assessment of readiness and of what cigars do for him; varenicline started now, before a quit date, with a plan to cut down and then stop; combination nicotine replacement (patch and lozenge) added from the quit date; cigars are counted like any other tobacco; weekly behavioral support by phone with the national quitline and in clinic; relapse treated as part of the process
  • Maxillofacial prosthodontics consultation for a worn, poorly sealing obturator with pain, hypernasal speech and nasal leakage, and for dental care
  • Head and neck cancer survivorship: yearly examination of the mouth, defect and neck by his head and neck surgeon (more than five years after treatment), self-examination of the mouth, prompt review of any sore, lump, bleeding or change that lasts two weeks, imaging only for symptoms, and counseling on the risk of second primary cancers of the mouth, throat, larynx, esophagus and lung, which stopping smoking lowers
  • Chronic pain: scheduled acetaminophen up to 3,000 mg a day, a well-fitting obturator, warm saline rinses, and no long-term opioids; the plan is reviewed at each visit with a pain score
  • Nutrition: dietitian advice on soft high-protein meals, oral nutrition supplements twice daily, weight at each visit and albumin rechecked
  • Prosthodontic care: chairside reline and flange adjustment now, a new definitive obturator, nightly cleaning and an overnight soak, high-fluoride toothpaste, dental cleaning every three months, nicotine lozenge rather than gum, and speech and swallowing therapy sessions with a speech-language pathologist after the reline
  • Cardiovascular risk: lipid panel and 10-year risk estimate; a statin discussed with him once the smoking plan is under way

resource.title: Sigmund Freud synthetic care plan
resource.description: Treating tobacco dependence in a man who has already had a smoking-related cancer, without judgment: primary care for a 74-year-old physician and writer, seven years after a partial maxillectomy for squamous cell carcinoma of the palate, who still smokes about twenty cigars a day after many failed attempts to stop. The episode covers an assessment of readiness that does not blame him; starting varenicline before he is ready to set a quit date and adding combination nicotine replacement (ATS 2020, USPSTF 2021), with the point that cigars count; behavioral support; the risk of second primary cancers; head and neck cancer survivorship (NCCN, ACS 2016): yearly examination after five years, imaging only for symptoms or as screening supports, and lung cancer screening eligibility when the history is of cigars rather than cigarettes; maxillofacial prosthodontic care of the obturator, with speech, swallowing and dental care; nutrition and weight; and chronic pain managed without long-term opioids (CDC 2022). There is no radiation in the synthetic history, so there is no osteoradionecrosis risk.
